question.prompt: Emmy says to Max, “I ordered \(36\) math club sweatshirts today.” Max asks, “How much did each shirt cost?” Emmy responds, “I’ll give you a hint. The total cost was \(\$\underline{A}\,\underline{B}\,\underline{B}.\underline{B}\,\underline{A},\) where \(A\) and \(B\) are digits and \(A \neq 0.\)” After a pause, Max says, “That was a good price.” What is \(A + B?\)

solutions.title: Use divisibility rules
solutions.explanation:
Under the usual assumption of a common whole-cent price per sweatshirt, converting the total to cents makes it a multiple of \(36\). Its digits are then \(\overline{ABBBA}\), so digit divisibility tests apply.

A multiple of \(36\) is divisible by both \(4\) and \(9\). Divisibility by \(9\) requires the digit sum
\[
2A+3B
\]
to be divisible by \(9\), and hence by \(3\). Since \(3B\) is divisible by \(3\), \(2A\), and therefore \(A\), must be divisible by \(3\).

Also, a multiple of \(4\) is even, so its last digit \(A\) is even. The only nonzero digit that is both even and divisible by \(3\) is \(6\). Thus \(A=6\).

The digit sum is now \(12+3B\). For this to be divisible by \(9\), \(B+4\) must be divisible by \(3\). Among the digits \(0\) through \(9\), this gives exactly
\[
B=2,5,8.
\]
Divisibility by \(4\) depends on the last two digits. The three possibilities are \(26\), \(56\), and \(86\), of which only \(56\) is divisible by \(4\). Therefore \(B=5\).

This pair works: \(65556=36\cdot1821\), corresponding to \(\$18.21\) per shirt. Hence
\[
A+B=6+5=\boxed{11},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutions.title: Reduce the place-value expression
solutions.explanation:
The place-value coefficients of the total are close to multiples of \(36\), allowing us to replace the five-digit total by a much smaller divisibility condition.

Assuming a common whole-cent price per sweatshirt, let \(T\) be the total in cents. Then
\[
T=10001A+1110B
\]
is divisible by \(36\). Since
\[
10001=36\cdot278-7,
\qquad
1110=36\cdot31-6,
\]
we can write
\[
T=36(278A+31B)-(7A+6B).
\]
The first term is already a multiple of \(36\), so \(T\) is divisible by \(36\) exactly when \(7A+6B\) is.

In particular, \(7A+6B\) must be divisible by \(6\). But
\[
7A+6B=6(A+B)+A,
\]
so \(A\) must be divisible by \(6\). Because \(A\) is a nonzero digit, \(A=6\).

The remaining condition is that
\[
42+6B=6(B+7)
\]
be divisible by \(36\), meaning \(B+7\) is divisible by \(6\). As \(0\le B\le9\), we have \(7\le B+7\le16\). The only multiple of \(6\) in this interval is \(12\), so \(B=5\).

Indeed, \(65556=36\cdot1821\), so the price is a whole number of cents. Therefore
\[
A+B=\boxed{11},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
